authorship.method: Hand-authored before consulting kanasim distances or generated weighted rankings.
authorship.bank: Approved Japanese practice bank from japaneseSemanticBank; no draft-only words admitted.
authorship.status: Frozen hypotheses; not human listening judgments.

policy.ties: Report separately; a tie does not satisfy a strict expected ordering. Do not silently break ties using item IDs for benchmark accuracy.
policy.unsupported: Report unsupported probes separately and retain them in the declared denominator; never drop them silently.
policy.invariants: Report correctness separately from exploratory ordering; identity checks are not evidence that one model predicts perception better.
policy.exploratory: Report wins, ties, reversals and unsupported counts, plus categories; these are provisional phonetic hypotheses rather than empirical listener labels.
policy.scope: Synthetic probes exercise sound behavior only. Approved-bank triplets test raw phonetic ordering before pack, picture-validity or threshold filtering; production-scoped coverage is a separate diagnostic.

triplets.reason: Hiragana and katakana versions must have zero distance; a changed consonant must remain distinct.
Half-width katakana must normalize to the same reading without collapsing a changed consonant.
An identical sequence must be closer than one with an additional vowel mora; do not erase duration contrasts.
An identical sequence must be closer than the geminate counterpart; small tsu must retain a nonzero cost.
Voicing can affect similarity but must not collapse distinct readings to zero distance.
Full-size ya and a small-ya glide must not become identical sequences.
The moraic nasal must not be discarded.
Same-reading compound spellings normalize to zero distance; a different sequence remains distinct. This does not establish pitch-accent identity.
The same-place stop voicing change is hypothesized closer than replacing the stop with a fricative.
The voiced counterpart of the initial fricative is hypothesized closer than a nasal replacement.
Changing only the nasal consonant is hypothesized closer than changing that consonant and the final vowel.
The front vowel change i to e is hypothesized closer than i to o; this is an exploratory feature-based expectation.
Preserving the palatalized consonant is hypothesized closer than replacing its entire initial mora. These strings are controlled sound probes, not vocabulary claims.
A single vowel-length insertion is hypothesized closer than a substantially different consonant/vowel sequence.
A gemination difference is hypothesized closer than changing both base morae; the length distinction must still remain nonzero.
Removing the final nasal is hypothesized closer than changing the base vowel and consonant sequence.
A shared initial mora with one remaining replacement is hypothesized closer than a two-mora replacement.
Keeping the final mora and initial vowel is hypothesized closer than replacing the full sequence.
Both alternatives share chi; retaining the initial u vowel is hypothesized closer than replacing it with i. This ordering needs listening validation.
Preserving the a-ma sequence with an initial consonant change is hypothesized closer than an unrelated vowel/consonant sequence.
Engineering and archeology share an ordered sound sequence with one inserted mora; their semantic relation is not part of the phonetic expectation.
The shared geminate-plus-kou ending is hypothesized closer than the different sequence in sankaku.
Keeping the long initial vowel and the first three morae is hypothesized closer than a largely different sequence.
The shared dai suffix and partial initial vowel match are hypothesized closer than the different evening reading.

listening.targetSelection: Predeclared from approved vocabulary without consulting either ranking.

targets.reason: Writing-only admission and known same-reading exclusion

design.comparison: For each target present the target audio followed by two methods’ top-three valid pronunciation alternatives. If the candidate sets are identical, record that as an unchanged set instead of inventing a preference.
design.blinding: Hide algorithm names, numeric distances and word meanings until choices are saved. Present only A/B labels and recordings; reveal textual readings only after rating or in a separate inspection view.
design.balance: Use opposite method-to-A/B assignments on the two voice passes for each target, with a fixed recorded seed/order. Use one common existing approved voice for target and alternatives within each trial, rotating two available native voices between passes.
design.prompt: Which group contains alternatives that sound more similar to the target, while remaining distinguishable?
design.analysis: Report each response category and voice separately, with the number of changed and unchanged sets. Do not convert missing, uncertain or neither responses into a win; no significance or learner-difficulty claim from a single reviewer.
